bull.t: Recurring subscription and premium revenue growth
bull.b: The rising subscription mix improves revenue visibility and reduces reliance on one-off licensing. Premium access growth and near-100% subscriber retention support customer lifetime value and strengthen the company’s recurring-revenue base.

Growth in editorial and custom solutions broadens Getty’s monetization beyond standard stock libraries. These offerings can deepen enterprise and media relationships, support differentiated pricing, and create durable demand for specialized visual content.

bull.t: Licensed content distribution and product innovation
bull.b: Verification, AI-enabled discovery, and expanded distribution address the industry’s shift toward generative tools and trusted content. Partnerships may increase library reach while product innovation helps preserve the value of licensed imagery.

bear.t: High leverage and weak cash generation
bear.b: Large debt balances, high-cost financing, and limited cash reduce financial flexibility. Negative free cash flow means operations are not currently funding the business, increasing dependence on refinancing, asset actions, or further balance-sheet measures.

bear.t: Structural pressure on agency, iStock, and subscribers
bear.b: Weak agency and microstock demand, generative-AI disruption, regional contraction, and a sharply smaller subscriber base threaten the company’s customer funnel. Lower retention also suggests that recurring-revenue gains may not fully offset underlying demand erosion.

The legal judgment creates a material cash and capital-allocation burden while appeals remain unresolved. Combined with suspended guidance and an ongoing financing review, the issue can constrain investment capacity and keep management focused on liquidity repair.
